documents.title: Inhaler

documents.body: My albuterol says it expired in February — I barely use it but want a fresh one before spring. Same pharmacy please.

documents.title: RE: Inhaler

events.reason: Hypotension and bronchospasm during dental procedure

conditions.label: Anaphylaxis
conditions.note: During a dental procedure; trigger not established

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PHYSICIAN RECORD
Visit date: 07/14/2023   Arrival 10:20 by EMS

CC: Low blood pressure and wheezing during dental work.

HPI: 34-year-old man with systemic mastocytosis, allergic asthma and allergic rhinitis. He was in the chair for a scheduled dental procedure when his blood pressure dropped suddenly and he began wheezing; office staff called EMS. Arrives hypotensive with bronchospasm. Inciting exposure not clear from the history available.

PMH: systemic mastocytosis; allergic asthma; persistent allergic rhinitis; generalized anxiety disorder.
PSH: tonsillectomy (childhood); third molar extraction.
Home meds: epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg PRN; cetirizine 10 mg daily; famotidine 20 mg BID; albuterol HFA PRN; fluticasone nasal daily; cromolyn oral solution 200 mg QID.
Allergies: Hymenoptera venom (anaphylaxis), latex (anaphylaxis), dust mite, Timothy grass pollen.
Social: never smoker, occasional alcohol, teaches high school math.
Family: father with severe sting allergy and hypertension; paternal uncle with systemic mastocytosis.

Vitals on arrival: BP 84/52, HR 116, RR 24, SpO2 92% RA.

Exam: alert. Expiratory wheeze throughout. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft. Skin warm.

ED course: Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM to the anterolateral thigh at 10:24. Within about 15 minutes pressure up to 116/74, HR 102, wheeze cleared and breathing comfortably. No further doses needed. Monitored on telemetry for observation; remained stable.

Discharge vitals: BP 124/78, HR 88, SpO2 98% RA.

Impression: Anaphylaxis during a dental procedure; trigger not established.

Disposition: Home at 16:05 on his usual regimen. Carry both auto-injectors. Follow up with PCP this week. Return for any recurrence of symptoms.

Allergies reviewed: venom, latex.

documents.title: Call from patient
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Randall called my cell from home. Had a reaction in the dentist's chair this morning — pressure dropped, wheezing — EMS took him to the ED, got IM epi there and improved quickly. Home since 4, feels wiped out but breathing fine. No recurrence. Reviewed: if any return of symptoms, use the auto-injector and call 911, don't wait. Booked him Wednesday. Asked him to bring the ED paperwork.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED follow-up.

Friday 7/14: anaphylaxis in the dental chair — hypotension and bronchospasm, IM epinephrine x1 in the ED with quick recovery, observed ~6 h, home same day. ED record received and reviewed. Trigger not established.

Since then: no recurrence. Tired for a day, back to normal now. Has not reused albuterol. Taking cetirizine, famotidine and cromolyn as usual.

His auto-injectors at home are past their date. New prescription today.

GAD-7 9, PHQ-9 4 — a bit more on edge this week, understandable; not asking for treatment.

Allergies: Hymenoptera venom, latex (anaphylaxis); dust mite; Timothy grass.

Exam: well, no distress. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Heart regular. Skin clear.

A/P:
1. Anaphylaxis 7/14 — resolved. Epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg two-pack sent; carry both.
2. Systemic mastocytosis — regimen unchanged.
3. Allergic asthma — quiet.
4. GAD — slightly up after the event, follow at the physical next month.
He'll let the dental office know about this episode before rescheduling.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. 34M.

Since the July ED visit for anaphylaxis during dental work, no further reactions. Picked up the new auto-injectors. School starts next week.

Asthma: no albuterol since spring. Rhinitis: controlled on daily fluticasone.
SM: same regimen, cetirizine/famotidine/oral cromolyn.
GAD-7 7, back near his usual.

Meds and allergies reviewed, no changes. Never smoker, AUDIT-C 1.

Exam: HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen benign, no organomegaly. Skin unremarkable. Neuro intact.

Plan:
- CBC, CMP.
- Flu and updated COVID vaccine in October.
- Continue current meds.
- Next physical August.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your CBC and metabolic panel are normal across the board. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza (quad) 0.5 mL IM L deltoid; 2023-24 COVID (Pfizer) 0.3 mL IM R deltoid. Latex-free supplies, chart flag confirmed. Auto-injectors with him. Observed 15 min without incident.

documents.title: Missed you yesterday
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Randall, we missed you at your 4:00 follow-up yesterday. Want to rebook? Video works too if after-school is tight.

documents.title: RE: Missed you yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So sorry — staff meeting ran way over and I completely forgot. Video would be great, any afternoon after 3:30 the first week of March.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home. Identity confirmed.

Asthma: one albuterol use all winter. No cough at night.
Rhinitis: fine on fluticasone.
SM: no reactions since July. Allergist saw him in the fall, regimen the same.
Anxiety: GAD-7 6. Busy but manageable. Declines treatment again, which is reasonable at this level.

Meds reviewed, unchanged. Allergies unchanged.

Assessment: allergic asthma and rhinitis controlled; systemic mastocytosis stable; GAD mild.
Plan: continue all. Physical in August.

documents.title: EpiPens
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Both my auto-injectors expire next month. Could you send a new two-pack before I head out for summer stuff? Thanks!

documents.title: RE: EpiPens
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sent a new two-pack to your pharmacy. Insurance covered it with the usual copay. Keep the old ones until the new ones are in hand.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam — 35 y/o male teacher.

Quiet year. No reactions, no urgent visits. Auto-injectors renewed in June. Albuterol barely used. Nasal symptoms controlled. Keeps cromolyn going faithfully.

Screens: GAD-7 7, PHQ-9 2, AUDIT-C 1. Never smoker.

Medications: cetirizine 10 mg daily; famotidine 20 mg BID; cromolyn oral solution 200 mg QID; fluticasone nasal 2 sprays/nostril daily; albuterol HFA PRN; epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector x2.
Allergies: Hymenoptera venom — anaphylaxis; latex — anaphylaxis; dust mite; Timothy grass.

Exam: Healthy-appearing. Eyes, ears, throat normal. No lymphadenopathy. Cardiac exam regular, no murmurs. Lungs clear, no wheezing. Abdomen nontender, no masses. Skin without rash. Normal gait and strength.

Plan: CBC and CMP today. Vaccines in the fall. Tdap due in 2026. All meds continued.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Randall, your labs from Wednesday are all within normal limits. See you in the fall for shots.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu (trivalent) right arm, 2024-25 COVID left arm. Latex-free. 15-minute wait, no problems.
